findings.issue: Recovery behaviour encoded as magic string prefixes (credential-store:, registry:, session-store:, operational:) prepended by constructors (176-302) and sniffed back by explicit_recovery (423) in fix_hint; five failure classes share CONFIG_INVALID/INPUT_INVALID with no type distinction; direct ConfigInvalid{detail} silently gets the check.toml hint.
findings.recommendation: Typed recovery field (ConfigInvalid{kind: ConfigKind, detail, recovery}) or separate variants sharing code(); keep wire code stable; restrict plain constructor.

findings.issue: Cause chains discarded at every boundary: JevError derives Clone/PartialEq/Eq with String fields only, no #[source], no From impls; five identical map_err(|_| InputInvalid{"response JSON could not be encoded"}) at 559/577/587/601/607; sc-jev-py error.rs:22-23 swallows setattr with let _; extract/read.rs:33-35 same for non-UTF-8; sc-treesitter extract.rs:257 reports InputTooLarge for line/offset overflow.
findings.recommendation: Sanitized helper JevError::encode_failed(label,&serde_json::Error) or typed variants keeping redaction; own variant for overflow.

findings.issue: Rev is a validation-free String newtype. sc-jev-check extract/read.rs:81 passes --end-of-options but sc-treesitter git_io.rs:27-28 formats {rev}:{path} into git show/rev-parse with no --end-of-options and no leading-dash check (a --rev starting with '-' parses as a git option). Repo-relative path validation implemented three times with different rules (read.rs:38, git_io.rs:56, sc-ai command.rs:740); paths cross crates as raw String.
findings.recommendation: Fallible Rev::parse rejecting empty/leading -/NUL/whitespace; RepoRelativePath newtype in sc-agent-types owning the one validator; all git calls through one helper with --end-of-options.

findings.issue: BackendId has no FromStr; parsing re-implemented in three places with different behaviour (caller.rs:110; sc-ai command.rs:687 via serde_json::from_value; sc-jev-py run.rs:135 accepting hyphen aliases, returning registry_invalid). CLI and Python accept different inputs. Backends carried as Vec<String> until late.
findings.recommendation: impl FromStr for BackendId/BackendKeyId with one error mapping; parse at the edge; decide whether hyphen aliases are contract.

findings.issue: SessionStore documented as open extension point but claim is false: RunOptions.sessions is concrete FileSessionStore; run_request calls inherent open/load/record_outcome not on the trait; one implementor. registry/mod.rs:3-5 docs have the same shape.
findings.recommendation: Delete the trait, or move open/load/record_outcome onto it and make RunOptions dyn/generic; document the decision accurately.

findings.issue: Near-duplicate injection traits: sc-jev RetryDelay/ThreadRetryDelay/JevTransport/WireRequest vs sc-jev-backends RetrySleeper/ThreadSleeper/BackendTransport/HttpRequest. Retry-After parsing drifted (f64 seconds accepting fractions, inf/NaN->30s vs i64 clamp); busy status list duplicated. Each trait has one production impl.
findings.recommendation: One retry policy and, if feasible, one send trait in a shared crate/module; generics instead of Arc<dyn> for single production type; else ADR + pinning tests.

findings.issue: Canonical payload cloned ~5 times per backend: JudgeRequest owns PayloadBundle (clone per backend line 410), run_request clones into payloads (296), reloads and re-parses the session file every loop iteration for prior (289), clones bundle into CheckResult (323); backends body.to_vec() (170) and ResolvedApiKey clone per HttpRequest incl. retries (174); prepare called twice per judge (82-89); validate_for_send by caller (275,298) and again inside judge. same_bytes at 317 compares clones of one bundle with itself so equal_input.equal can never be false.
findings.recommendation: JudgeRequest<'a> borrowing or Arc<[u8]>; keep prior in memory; body as Arc<[u8]>/Cow; compute Prepared once; compute equal-input from what each backend actually received or drop the tautological check.

findings.issue: FileSessionStore hides mutable shared state behind &self: registry Arc<RwLock<BackendRegistry>> written by install_registry (150) as a side effect of every run_request (run/mod.rs:270), so a later ask depends on an earlier call; io Arc<Mutex<()>> is process-local and does not protect CLI + Python concurrently; poison swallowed.
findings.recommendation: Pass registry at construction or make ask take &BackendRegistry (RwLock goes away); document cross-process out of scope or add OS advisory lock; RBP-006 rationale comments.

findings.issue: Sealed Extractor trait and extractor_for() unused in production: extract_input dispatches with a match; extractor_for referenced only by a unit test; trait cannot express extract_with_source.
findings.recommendation: Remove trait and extractor_for, or route extract_input through it and fold extract_with_source in.

findings.issue: ResolvedApiKey::new accepts anything; normalized_typesafe/normalized_provider must be remembered by each backend constructor; trimmed twice; plain String cloned freely with no zeroize; redact_error handles four variants by substring replacement.
findings.recommendation: Fallible ResolvedApiKey::try_new(backend, String); drop post-hoc normalized_*; Arc<str> or zeroizing buffer.

findings.issue: PayloadBundle pub bytes + pub sha256 allow mismatched literal; LogEvent.operation String 'judge'/'ask'; Question.id / ChoiceAnswer.question_id separate Strings; schema/mode/blob_sha/rev raw strings validated ad hoc; equal_input::record takes two adjacent bools.
findings.recommendation: Private fields with accessors; operation enum; QuestionId and BlobSha newtypes (reuse 40-hex validator); enums for mode/schema; struct instead of two bools.

findings.issue: ~190-line hand-rolled argv parser with parallel Flags/RunCommand/AskCommand structs, stringly typed until dispatch, two flag tables (parse_flags and assign) maintained separately.
findings.recommendation: clap derive into typed fields, or at least merge flag tables and parse typed values in parse_flags.

findings.issue: Duplicate SessionLog-to-sc-observability adapter in sc-ai observe.rs and sc-jev-py logging.rs with divergent error mapping (operational_config vs session_store_io for same failure) and env precedence (SC_LOG_ROOT vs SC_AGENT_LOG_DIR).
findings.recommendation: Shared adapter module; each root supplies only path policy; normalize error constructor.

findings.issue: SessionLog public trait with no stated seal/open decision (three impls across crates).
findings.recommendation: One doc sentence stating intentionally open and why.

findings.issue: run/mod.rs 1050 lines (~635 inline tests from 415); session/mod.rs 738 (tests from 548); run/exact.rs (430) is an integration test compiled via [[test]] path=src/run/exact.rs instead of tests/; hand-built ConfigInvalid/InputInvalid literals at run/mod.rs:252,386 and session/mod.rs:348-356 bypass typed constructors and get the wrong hint.
findings.recommendation: Move exact.rs to tests/; split inline test modules to run/tests.rs and session/tests.rs; dedicated constructors for run-request/follow-up validation.

notes: review_mode phase_review treated as phase_end; send phase_end in future
Object safety fine on all traits; issue is duplication/unused abstraction
Serde hygiene generally good (deny_unknown_fields on wire types, kebab-case consistent); SessionDocument/JudgeOutcome/EqualInputRecord lack deny_unknown_fields (not raised)
Single JevError enum with stable code()/fix_hint() is a strength
Not reviewed in depth: sc-jev check.rs, sc-jev-backends wire.rs/validate.rs, sc-jev-check payload/, config/mod.rs, extract/{table,command,subjects}.rs bodies, sc-jev-py run.rs beyond line 260
